description: Wire-level call-pattern matrix (FIX_PLAN.md §5). Every case here MUST be executed exactly once by scripts/wire/run.mjs and produce a recorded pass/fail result — a case declared here but never executed by a driver is itself a suite failure (T1: 'CANNOT silently skip'). The floor on case count is enforced independently in scripts/wire/run.mjs (not read from this file), so an empty or truncated manifest cannot pass trivially (QA binding finding 3).

A discarded connect() promise against a REAL dead port must NOT crash the Node process via an unhandled promise rejection — driven in an isolated child process so a real crash cannot take the rest of the wire suite down with it

cases.pattern: useMinder('/ad-hoc-axios-config', { axiosConfig: { url: 'http://<attacker-host>/exfil' } }) — the real public hook, no direct apiClient.request() call
cases.description: SECURITY (fourth channel, END-TO-END public-API reachability): useMinder.ts's axiosConfig passthrough on an unregistered path-shaped route reaches requestRaw exactly like the direct apiClient.request() cases above. Must never touch EITHER server and must surface the refusal as a query failure (success:false, error set), not silently dispatch.

cases.pattern: two concurrent apiClient.request(routeName, undefined, undefined, { params }) calls with DIFFERENT params on the SAME GET route, deduplication enabled
cases.description: DEDUP KEY DIVERGENCE (genuinely exercised, not just refused): the reported repro — two concurrent GETs differing only in params ({q:'alpha'}/{q:'beta'}) used to collapse into ONE wire request (params was never in the cache key) and hand BOTH callers the same response. Must dispatch as TWO separate wire requests and each caller must receive the response matching its OWN request.

cases.pattern: two concurrent apiClient.request(routeName, undefined, undefined, { headers }) calls with DIFFERENT per-call headers on the SAME GET route, deduplication enabled
cases.description: DEDUP KEY DIVERGENCE, CHANNEL 2 (cross-tenant disclosure): the reported repro verbatim — two concurrent GETs differing only in a per-call header ({'X-User':'alice'}/{'X-User':'bob'}) used to collapse into ONE wire request under per-request auth ("bob received alice's response"). Must dispatch as TWO separate wire requests, each carrying its own caller's header.

cases.pattern: standalone minder('registeredRoute', undefined, { baseURL: '<attacker-host>' }) with a registered route declaring its own X-Api-Key header and an ambient bearer token set via minder.config({ token })
cases.description: BLOCKER 1 (fix-2.2.0-blockers): the identical exfiltration the ApiClient choke point already refuses, reopened through the standalone minder() path, which builds its axios config by hand-picking fields rather than spreading options. Must return success:false (minder() never throws by default) before dispatch — zero requests reach EITHER server, and neither the route's X-Api-Key header nor the ambient bearer token ever reaches the attacker host.

cases.pattern: createTypedMinder({...}).minder(key, undefined, { baseURL: '<attacker-host>' }) — the public typed-routes wrapper, not a direct minder() call
cases.description: BLOCKER 1, END-TO-END PUBLIC-API REACHABILITY: createTypedMinder(...).minder() (src/core/typedRoutes.ts) delegates straight into minder() — proves that delegation actually inherits the fix rather than bypassing it through a second, untouched entry point. Same assertions as the direct minder() case: success:false, zero requests to either server, no header/token leak.

cases.pattern: two concurrent apiClient.request(routeName, undefined, undefined, { params, paramsSerializer }) calls with the SAME params but DIFFERENT paramsSerializer functions, deduplication enabled
cases.description: SHOULD-FIX 3 (fix-2.2.0-blockers): paramsSerializer is on the forwardable allowlist and is wire-affecting (it changes the encoded query string), but the previous JSON.stringify(requestConfig) dedup key silently dropped function-valued fields, so two calls differing only in paramsSerializer collapsed into ONE wire request. Must dispatch as TWO separate wire requests, each reflecting its OWN caller's serialized query string.

RELEASE BLOCKER, EXACT REPRODUCTION: route /users/:id, standalone minder('updateUser', body, { params: { id: '..' } }) previously sent PUT / (the SITE ROOT) carrying the full attacker-controlled body, with success:true and no throw. Must now report success:false (error.code=UNSAFE_ROUTE_PARAM_VALUE), zero requests reach the wire.

RELEASE BLOCKER, EXACT REPRODUCTION: route /t/:id/comments, standalone minder(..., { params: { id: '5#' } }) previously sent PUT /t/5 (the PARENT resource) plus a redundant/leaking '?id=5%23' query param. Must now refuse before dispatch, zero requests reach the wire.

RELEASE BLOCKER, EXACT REPRODUCTION: route /flat/:id, standalone minder(..., { params: { id: '5?a=1' } }) previously sent PUT /flat/5?a=1&id=5%3Fa%3D1 — a LIVE caller-controlled query param ('a=1') merged onto the real request, targeting a different resource/semantics than intended. Must now refuse before dispatch, zero requests reach the wire.

RELEASE BLOCKER, EXACT REPRODUCTION: route /users/:id, standalone minder(..., { params: { id: '' } }) previously sent PUT /users/?id= — the COLLECTION, not the single resource the caller intended. Must now refuse before dispatch, zero requests reach the wire.

RELEASE BLOCKER: a percent-encoded traversal sequence in a standalone minder() route param must be caught after bounded percent-decoding, mirroring the CRUD-path F4 coverage in crud-id-hostile-inputs.mjs — zero requests reach the wire.

RELEASE BLOCKER: the standalone-minder()-path mirror of crud-id-hostile-inputs.mjs's F5 bare-dot case — route /dot-standalone/:id, { params: { id: '.' } } must now refuse before dispatch (zero requests reach the wire), proving the SAME shared choke point closes this gap for options.params too.
RELEASE BLOCKER: a single-encoded '.' (lowercase hex) supplied via options.params must be refused after decoding, zero requests reach the wire.
RELEASE BLOCKER: a single-encoded '.' (uppercase hex digit) supplied via options.params must be refused after decoding, zero requests reach the wire.
RELEASE BLOCKER: a double-encoded '.' supplied via options.params must be refused once the bounded decode loop fully resolves it to a bare dot-segment, zero requests reach the wire.
RELEASE BLOCKER: three dots supplied via options.params — nothing-but-dots of any length — must be refused before dispatch, zero requests reach the wire.
POSITIVE CONTROL: the legitimate numeric param 0 on the standalone minder() path must still dispatch PUT /pos-zero-standalone/0 with success:true — a guard that refuses valid input is its own defect.
POSITIVE CONTROL: a leading-zero string param ('007') on the standalone minder() path must still dispatch PUT /pos-007-standalone/007 with success:true.
POSITIVE CONTROL: a UUID param on the standalone minder() path must still dispatch correctly (hyphens are not in the hostile character class).

cases.pattern: minder('posNestedStandalone', undefined, { params: { id: '42' } }) on route /pos-t-standalone/:id/comments
cases.description: POSITIVE CONTROL: a nested route with a genuine ':id' PATH placeholder and a valid id on the standalone minder() path must still dispatch GET /pos-t-standalone/42/comments with success:true.

REGRESSION GUARD: a ':id' route substituted via the standalone minder() + options.params path must substitute the id into the URL PATH ONLY — no redundant/leaking '?id=...' query string appended alongside it (the minder.ts consumedKeys exclusion fix, mirroring ApiClient.dispatchResolved's existing consumedKeys filtering).

BLOCKER 2: the provider upload path (ApiClient.uploadFile -> dispatchNativeFetch) dispatches via native fetch() with a real multipart body when transport:'fetch' is set — axios's own request/response pipeline is never invoked

BLOCKER 2, SIMULATED bare workerd (fetch stub throws on any RequestInit.cache field, per the wave brief's own fallback instruction): the provider upload still completes a real multipart round trip — the native-fetch dispatch never sets 'cache'

BLOCKER 2: standalone minder()'s file-upload branch honours an EXPLICIT transport:'fetch' instead of always forcing axios (isComplexRequest previously overrode it unconditionally) — dispatches via native fetch() with a real multipart body
BLOCKER 2, SIMULATED bare workerd (fetch stub throws on any RequestInit.cache field): standalone minder()'s file upload still completes a real multipart round trip under transport:'fetch'

FAILURE PATH: a provider upload under transport:'fetch' against a REAL dead port reports a clean, network-shaped failure — no crash, and not the workerd-style RequestInit error masquerading as something else

HIGH: the provider path under transport:'fetch' sends content-type: application/json for a plain JSON body, matching standalone minder()'s existing behaviour — previously sent text/plain;charset=UTF-8 because dispatchNativeFetch never merged in the axios instance's own default headers

FAILURE PATH: standalone minder() against a REAL dead port, with configureMinder({offline:{enabled:true}}), reports success:false (error.code=OFFLINE_ERROR) AND the failed mutation lands in getOfflineManager()'s queue -- previously reported NETWORK_ERROR with queueSize 0

KNOWN LIMITATION (discovered building this driver, not H1/H1b -- those are about the ENQUEUE side, proven by the case above): standalone has no baseURL-aware requestExecutor wired for OfflineManager replay (unlike the provider path), so sync() for a standalone-queued relative URL fails with a clean 'Failed to parse URL' stat instead of crashing/hanging -- documents the gap honestly, flagged as a follow-up rather than silently asserting replay success

HOSTILE INPUT / regression guard: the SAME real dead-port failure with NO offline config still reports a plain NETWORK_ERROR and never starts queueing -- the broadened no-response classification is gated on offline support actually being enabled
HOSTILE INPUT: a real dead-port failure for a GET-method standalone minder() call, with offline support enabled, is NEVER auto-queued -- only mutations are queueable

cases.pattern: standalone minder() + <MinderDataProvider> useMinder().mutate(), same configureMinder instance
cases.description: H1b proof: a standalone minder() failure and a <MinderDataProvider>+useMinder().mutate() failure, against the SAME configureMinder-wired instance and dead port, land in the SAME OfflineManager queue (2 entries) -- proves one shared failure-classification choke point, not two independently-matching implementations

cases.pattern: minder() from a fresh module graph, ESM root entry
cases.description: a bare minder() call against a REAL dead port, from a FRESH process where no plugin has ever been registered (the common App Router Route Handler/Server Component case), returns a MinderResult (success:false) -- never throws, never crashes the process

cases.pattern: minder() from a fresh module graph, CJS ./node entry
cases.description: the SAME never-throws contract through the Node-targeted ./node subpath a server-only Route Handler would plausibly import from

cases.pattern: 3 sequential minder() calls, same warm process
cases.description: root-cause proof: the fix is not a one-shot accident of module-init ordering -- repeated minder() calls in the same warm process (matching serverless/App-Router function reuse) all return a clean MinderResult with no throw

cases.description: SECURITY (redirect header leak, standalone path): a real 302 from the route's own trusted host to a SECOND, independent server must still dispatch successfully, but axios's sensitiveHeaders (now set from the route's own declared header names via the shared choke point src/core/apiClient/sensitiveHeaders.ts) must strip the route's static X-Api-Key header on the cross-origin redirect hop -- the first hop receives it normally, the redirect target never does
registered PUT route, params substitution -- standalone minder() and provider ApiClient must dispatch byte-identical PUT /items/7 requests

URLSearchParams body under the default (axios) transport -- both entry points must form-encode identically
FormData body under the default (axios) transport -- both entry points must produce the same multipart encoding (random boundary token normalised before comparison)
a route's own declared static header (X-Api-Key) must reach the wire identically from both entry points
security.sanitization applied to a request body field -- regression guard for the previously-fixed sanitization no-op, both entry points must sanitize identically
security.sanitization applied to a GET query param -- both entry points must sanitize identically
a registered route with the SAME :id placeholder repeated twice in its URL template must substitute identically on both entry points

hostile-route-params failure path: a percent-encoded dot-segment ('%2e%2e') on a registered route must be refused with zero wire requests on both entry points
an explicit GET with a request body -- both entry points must dispatch it identically
options.params on an UNREGISTERED path -- documents a SHARED defect (both entry points leave the literal :id placeholder unsubstituted on the wire), not a standalone-vs-provider divergence

failure path (4xx): outgoing request shape parity when the server answers 404 -- response-side error-vocabulary divergence is documented in the case message, out of this comparator's {method,path,body,headers} scope
